facing_object.object_name: Light-gray armchair further from the wall painting
facing_object.description: A light-gray upholstered armchair with a cushioned seat and back, and a blue rectangular throw pillow. It is one of two similar armchairs placed by a large arched window. The 'wall painting' is a circular, colorful (predominantly blue and green) mosaic art piece on the wall to the left of the front door (when entering). This armchair is the one positioned more to the right side of the window area (further from the wall with the mosaic) when viewing from the front door.

question: Imagine you are a robot standing by the dark wooden front door and facing the light-gray armchair further from the wall painting, when the speech topic: "offering the listener's coffee" comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the speaker: left, right, or back? If the object is generally to your left and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees left, choose 'left'. If the object is generally to your right and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees right, choose 'right'. If the object is generally behind you and facing it requires turning 120 degrees or more, choose 'back'.
